title: That Awful Day Will Surely Come
description: That Awful Day Will Surely Come in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 107, headed “The everlasting absence of God intolerable”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: That aw-ful day will sure-ly come, Th'ap-point-ed hour makes haste, When I must stand be-fore my Judge, And pass the sol-emn test.

lines: That awful day will surely come,
When I must stand before my Judge,
Thou lovely chief of all my joys,
How could I bear to hear thy voice
The thunder of that dismal word,
What, to be banish'd from my life,
O wretched state of deep despair,
And fix my doleful station where
I must not taste his Love.
Jesus, I throw my arms around,
Without a gracious smile from thee
O tell me that my worthless name
Shew me some promise in thy book
Give me one kind assuring word,
And cheerfully my soul shall wait

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
